spec_match.rationale: The dual-signature concept is genuinely demonstrated via the backend verifier, but the 'assertion structure' sample invents a `response.browserBoundKey {publicKey, signature, attestation}` field — the spec surfaces it as getClientExtensionResults().payment.browserBoundSignature.signature (verified against w3c.github.io/secure-payment-confirmation#sctn-browser-bound-key-store).

interactive.rationale: The Run dual-signature verifier button performs a real enroll → challenge → sign → server-verify roundtrip against the showcase backend (verified end-to-end via CDP click: enrollment stored, payload issued, both signatures verified).

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises a support check, backend-backed dual-signature verification, and the assertion-shape explanation; the page delivers all three.

edge_cases.rationale: Only the happy path runs: the click handler has no try/catch (a backend failure becomes an unhandled rejection with the output stuck on 'Running…') and no tampered-signature negative case is shown.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5106102997614592, the W3C SPC spec, and the sibling key-management concept.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite checks broad SPC prerequisites (PaymentRequest, PublicKeyCredential, crypto.subtle) and passes 6/6 even in this pre-145 browser — it cannot observe any browser-bound-key-specific contract, so it proves prerequisites rather than the feature.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Support rows render honest states and the backend verifier flow was driven and verified in headless Chromium 141 with a clean console; the real SPC browser-bound-key path needs a payment credential and Chrome support, so it cannot be observed here.

telemetry_health.rationale: Server-injected /public/demo-telemetry.js verified in the served DOM (errors, rejections, interactions, web vitals).

design_system.rationale: Design-system variables throughout; ok/err states use --accent-emerald/--accent-rose on paper backgrounds.

accessibility.rationale: The verifier button is a native labelled button, but support-row values and the output pre update without any live region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-measured at 360px: content reaches 399px because .support-label reserves min-width:16rem, pushing the support values past the viewport where body overflow-x:hidden clips them.

openQuestions.title: Correct the assertion-structure sample to the spec shape
openQuestions.detail: The spec (sctn-browser-bound-key-store) returns the browser-bound signature as clientExtensionResults.payment.browserBoundSignature.signature, with the browser-bound public key conveyed via the payment extension at creation time — not a response.browserBoundKey {publicKey, signature, attestation} member. Rewrite the sample (and the 'New in Chrome 145' comment) to the real structure so developers don't code against an invented field.

openQuestions.title: Handle verifier failures and add a negative case
openQuestions.detail: Wrap the run-bbk-flow handler in try/catch with a visible error state, and add a tampered-signature branch that shows server-side verification returning false — the security property being demonstrated is only convincing when the failure branch is shown.

openQuestions.title: Fix mobile clipping of support values
openQuestions.detail: At 360px the .support-label min-width:16rem forces support values to 399px where they are clipped. Let the rows wrap (flex-wrap or a smaller label min-width at narrow widths).

summary: The live backend dual-signature verifier is real and works end-to-end (verified via CDP click), and API-support rows degrade honestly. The headline defect is the invented response.browserBoundKey assertion shape, which contradicts the spec's payment-extension browserBoundSignature output; mobile also clips the support values. Browser-verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshot + DOM dump) and raw CDP (real click dispatch, console/network capture, 360x740 DPR3 mobile emulation) — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session. Chromium 141 predates Chrome 145, so v145-only API paths were validated on their fallback branches, not the new-API success path. The single failed fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet request is environmental (blocked host) and was not counted against any page.
